prompt.title: Write it, then see it
prompt.chapterReference: Habit 2: Begin with the End in Mind
prompt.text: Pick a moment where you keep reacting in a way you don't like. Write one sentence about the person you are in that moment instead. Then spend a minute a day picturing it, in detail, before it happens.
prompt.glossText: The book calls the sentence an affirmation and the daily picturing visualization. Together they rewrite the response before the moment arrives.
prompt.whyItMatters: Deciding to be calmer doesn't survive contact with a slammed door. Having already seen yourself calm, in that hallway, with that face, does. Athletes rehearse this way; so can you.

list.empty: Nothing yet. Think of the last time you reacted and wished you hadn't.

form.textPrompt: One sentence: who are you in that moment? Present tense, and what you do rather than what you stop.
form.textPlaceholder: e.g. When my son slams the door, I breathe out, lower my voice and ask what happened.
form.scenePrompt: Picture it: where you are, who's there, what you feel.
form.scenePlaceholder: e.g. The hallway after school. His bag on the floor. My shoulders drop and I feel steady.
form.incompleteHint: Tick all five before you practise.

check.positiveLabel: It says what I do, not what I stop
check.positiveHint: "I lower my voice", not "I don't shout".
check.presentHint: "I breathe out", not "I will try to".
check.visualHint: A place, a face, a movement you could film.
check.emotionalHint: Name the feeling: calm, warm, steady.

practice.title: Practise
practice.hint: Close your eyes if you can. See the place, the faces, and yourself doing it. Feel it.
practice.finishedText: Time's up. Tap Done when you're ready.

guide.inShort: You'll write one sentence about who you are in a moment you keep getting wrong, check it against five qualities, and picture it for a minute a day. Two minutes to write; one a day to practise.
howTo: Tap "Add affirmation". Name the moment and write who you are in it, in one sentence.
Tick the five qualities. If one doesn't fit, change the sentence until it does.
Add the scene: where, who, what you feel. The more you can see, the better it works.
Tap "Practise", pick a length, press Start and picture it with your eyes closed.
Do it daily, ideally before the moment tends to happen. Tap "Mark done" after your first practice.

guide.afterwards: After a week, notice the moment itself: did the picture come to mind before you reacted? Adjust the sentence, not the goal. When it becomes how you actually respond, archive it and write the next one.
